result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend headings plus whitespace and say when cards or rules would work better. B gives much more detail on spacing: the heading sits closer to its own section (asymmetric spacing), gap is owned by the container, values come from one scale, and labels stay tight to their inputs. B also explains more clearly how this reduces clutter, for example by avoiding nested surfaces and checking the form with the blur test. A adds a useful accessibility point about fieldset and legend but is thinner on spacing relationships. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend headings plus space and give reasonable alternatives. A goes further on spacing: it covers how the heading sits relative to the fields and sections, the rule that space within a section is smaller than space between, gap ownership, a spacing scale, label proximity and toggle touch targets. It also adds a useful blur check. B adds accessibility notes with fieldset and legend, and its 'when to change' guidance is slightly more concrete, but its spacing detail and its explanation of how clutter is reduced are thinner.
